title: Level a rack shelf by moving the one pull pin that is in the wrong hole
instruction: Level the shelf so it sits flat on all four of its pins.
context: Done by: stock clerks, tool-crib and warehouse workers, rack installers (O*NET 53-7065, 53-7062, 47-2031). Adjustable steel racks carry shelves on T-handle pull pins; one pin a hole off tilts the shelf and loads slide off. A loaded pin cannot be moved, so one arm holds the shelf off it while the other re-indexes it. Unlike TK-8XXV9N (shim under a base that stays put) and TK-V4KV84 (lift a crate, slide a block under), the support itself moves to another hole under a held load.
setup: World frame for this text: 'front' is the side nearer the robot, 'out' is distance from the arm bases away from the robot, 'left' and 'right' are from the robot's view, heights are above the table top, and the midline is halfway between the two arm bases. An adjustable steel rack. Two fixed dark grey steel uprights, each 260 mm front to back, 40 mm thick and 130 mm tall, centred 30 cm out from the arm bases; their inner faces are 230 mm apart, 115 mm either side of the midline. Each has two columns of 14 mm square through-holes, 21 and 39 cm out from the arm bases, at three levels with centres 60, 85 and 110 mm up. Four loose orange steel T-handle pull pins (40 g each): a round shank 10 mm across and 126 mm long, a collar 20 mm across and 4 mm thick, and a T-handle 14 mm wide, 5 mm thick and 34 mm tall (from 10 mm below the shank's axis to 24 mm above it), its centre 41 mm outside the upright's face. Each pin goes through a hole from the outside, collar against the upright, and sticks out 40 mm on the inside. A loose light blue painted shelf deck (0.4 kg): a board 240 mm front to back, 200 mm wide and 10 mm thick, centred on the midline 30 cm out from the arm bases, with a lip 15 mm deep and 15 mm tall along its front edge, and on the lip a dark round rail 12 mm across and 170 mm long on two 10 mm posts, its axis 41 mm above the board's underside. The shelf rests on the pins' inner ends. Lot A: the front-left pin is at level 1 (60 mm), the other three at level 2 (85 mm), and the shelf rests tilted down at its front-left corner, about 11 degrees. Lot B: the front-right pin is at level 3 (110 mm), the other three at level 2, and the shelf rests tilted, high at its front-right corner, about 8 degrees. Nothing else is on the table. Trials are run on lots A and B and averaged; the screenshot shows lot A.
scoring: A pin is seated at a level when its shank goes through the hole of its own column at that level: its axis within 4 mm of the hole's centre sideways and 6 mm up or down, within 10 degrees of square to the upright, and its collar within 4 mm of the upright's outer face. Score 0 for the whole trial if at any point any of the three pins that started at level 2 moves more than 5 mm along its hole, or more than 8 mm sideways or up or down, from where it started. Otherwise: 1.0 when all four pins are seated at level 2 and the shelf rests on them flat (within 2 degrees of level), its underside within 4 mm of 88 mm up, its centre within 15 mm of the midline and of 30 cm out from the arm bases, with no part of either gripper (fingers, gripper body or wrist) within 5 mm of the shelf or any pin, everything still for 1 s. 0.5 when all four pins are seated at level 2, the robot has let go (as above), the pins and the shelf are still, and the shelf is not on the table (its lowest point more than 20 mm up), but the shelf is not resting flat on them. 0 otherwise. Trials are run on each of lots A and B and averaged.
reset_notes: Push every pin home in its lot's holes (lot A: front-left pin at level 1, the rest at level 2; lot B: front-right pin at level 3, the rest at level 2), handles upright, then lay the shelf on the pins, rail at the front, and let it settle. Nothing is consumed. Run with -E object_jitter=0 and --epochs 2.
fidelity: A bench-scale steel rack: 10 mm T-handle pull pins in 14 mm square through-holes in 40 mm uprights, levels 25 mm apart; the shelf has a front rail to lift it by. Masses and friction (1.2) are simulator values. Pins sit 2 mm below their hole's centre and droop a few degrees under load. A fixed habit (always move the front-left pin) scores 1.0 in one lot and 0 in the other, so it averages 0.5; the lots do not stop a memorised replay of both layouts.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (mean of lots A and B); demo: 1.0 in each lot
